recommended_services: Primary Care Physician / General Practitioner (PCP / GP)
Urgent Care Clinic (if symptoms are acute but not life-threatening)
preparation_steps: Record when the physical symptoms started and what makes them better or worse
List all existing over-the-counter supplements or previous medical history
Prepare 2-3 specific questions regarding your daily functional limitations

recommended_services: Licensed Mental Health Counselor or Clinical Psychologist
Psychiatrist (for clinical evaluation and comprehensive assessment)
Community Mental Health Center / Support Services
preparation_steps: Note any changes in sleep patterns, appetite, energy, or concentration
Identify key stressors or life events preceding these feelings
Consider asking a trusted friend or family member to support your appointment scheduling

recommended_services: Primary Care Physician with Integrated Behavioral Health
Collaborative Care Team (Medical Practitioner + Psychological Counselor)
preparation_steps: Keep a combined physical and emotional symptom log for 3-5 days
Document whether emotional stress intensifies somatic physical discomfort
Bring a unified timeline to your primary care clinician for holistic review

recommended_services: Primary Care Consultation / General Health Checkup
Registered Nurse Health Advice Line (e.g. 104 or local health line)
Community Pharmacist or Health Educator for baseline inquiries
preparation_steps: Maintain a daily log noting when symptoms occur, their intensity, and duration
Observe if symptoms relate to meals, sleep, physical exertion, or stress
Return to screening when you have tracked specific details over several days

recommended_services: 24/7 Crisis Support Lifeline (Call or text 988 or 14416)
preparation_steps: Do not wait or drive yourself if you are feeling faint, confused, or severely ill
Notify someone nearby immediately of your situation
Keep your phone with you and stay in a safe, seated or lying position
